keywords.nuance: やっと expresses relief because something finally happened after waiting, struggling, or taking longer than expected. It usually implies the speaker feels the process was difficult or frustrating.
keywords.example: やっと宿題が終わった。

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Don't think of やっと as just 'finally.' It usually carries the feeling of relief after something took longer or was harder than expected. If there was no delay or struggle, expressions like ついに or simply もう may sound more natural depending on the situation.

questions.hint: The speaker has probably been waiting a long time.
questions.answer: I can finally go to Japan.

questions.prompt: 一時間探して、やっと鍵を見つけた。
questions.hint: The speaker searched for quite a while.
questions.answer: After searching for an hour, I finally found my keys.

questions.hint: The rain lasted longer than expected.

questions.prompt: 何度も練習して、やっとできるようになった。
questions.hint: The speaker practiced many times before succeeding.
questions.answer: After practicing many times, I finally became able to do it.

productionQuestions.hint: Express relief after completing something that took time.

referenceAnswers.answer: やっとこの本を読み終えた。
referenceAnswers.note: A natural way to say you finally finished reading a book.

referenceAnswers.answer: この本をやっと読み終えた。
referenceAnswers.note: Equally natural; placement changes the emphasis slightly.

productionQuestions.prompt: After waiting for two hours, the bus finally arrived.
productionQuestions.hint: Mention the waiting first, then use やっと.

referenceAnswers.answer: 二時間待って、やっとバスが来た。
二時間も待って、やっとバスが来た。
referenceAnswers.note: Adding も emphasizes how long the wait felt.

referenceAnswers.answer: やっとこの文法が分かった。
この文法がやっと分かった。
referenceAnswers.note: Equally natural with a different emphasis.

referenceAnswers.answer: 彼女はやっと試験に合格した。
彼女はやっと試験に受かった。
referenceAnswers.note: 受かる is a common conversational alternative to 合格する.
